# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +252
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness

# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for
#                           a terminal state first (Never-again: the leg
#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner

#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.

# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.

set -euo pipefail

out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound

poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)

# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m

poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then

concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +252
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness

# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for

#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays

#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push

# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi
  if [ "$a" -lt 1 ]; then a=1; fi

# pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder. The `pubspec=` output key name is
# kept (daily-publish report consumers read it), its value is the tag

  | grep -v '\^' | awk '{print $2}' | sed 's|refs/tags/||' \
  | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1 || true)

newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)
if [ "$newest" = "$published" ]; then

fi

tag="v$pubspec"

in_flight() { # $1 = human reason — the outcome is UNOBSERVED, never an alarm

  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.

  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is

  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run

      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')

      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}

concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

Confirmed: ci.yml's mint step carries an explicit `permissions: contents:write` least-privilege constraint (with a comment citing gh-1172 round-2 review). The new daily-publish.yml mint step omits `permissions` → the minted token receives all permissions granted to the App installation (per create-github-app-token v3 docs: "If permissions is not specified, the token will have all permissions granted to the App installation"). This is a deviation from the established, explicitly-documented least-privilege pattern in this repo. The re-arm needs only `contents: write`. → IMPORTANT (security / least privilege).

Second finding: the missing-secret failover claim. The PR says "without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm." But the app-token step would FAIL (input required: app-id) and kill the job before the verify step ever runs. In the main repo secrets exist so it works; in forks or if secrets are rotated away, the leg hard-fails at the mint step instead of running the classification + manual-fix alarm. → IMPORTANT.

Wait, actually let me double check create-github-app-token behavior with empty inputs: yes, it errors "Input required and not supplied: app-id" → step fails → job fails (no continue-on-error). So failover never reaches the script. Confirmed.

Third: after a successful re-arm whose run hasn't registered in the single re-read, the unchanged alarm instructs "Manual fix: re-push the tag" — but the leg already re-pushed it; the instruction is now misleading and an operator double-re-push could cut yet another tag object. Deliberate (byte-identical text is tested), but a SUGGESTION to note the re-arm in the alarm.

Fourth (SUGGESTION): success-branch pub.dev re-read loop duplicates the top-of-leg 3-read loop — extract a shared helper.

Fifth (SUGGESTION?): `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` on the verify step is redundant — the job-level env already sets `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` (line ~549 `env:` at job level). Yes! Looking at the workflow: the job has `env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` at job level, and the PR adds a step-level `env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` duplicating it. Only RELEASE_APP_TOKEN was needed. Minor duplication — SUGGESTION.

Sixth: The re-arm sleep/read: only `read_sleep` (10s) between push and re-read; GitHub run registration typically takes longer → the alarm path will frequently fire even when the re-arm worked, filing a spurious issue (self-filing) each day... wait no — if the re-arm succeeded and the run registers later, the daily fires ::error:: + exit 1 → self-files issue with manual instructions. Then next daily sees the fresh push run and heals → issue auto-closes? Per the description "the next daily re-verifies" — but the alarm DID fire, so an issue gets filed anyway. Hmm — does exit 1 in the pubdev leg self-file an issue? The header comment says "Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a manual-publish instruction". So in the common case (re-arm succeeds, registration lag > 10s), the leg will: re-arm, fail to see run after 10s, fire never_triggered → exit 1 → issue filed → next daily verifies green → presumably issue closed by the report. That means the self-heal as implemented will still file a noisy manual-fix issue in exactly the scenario it was built to heal. Is that acceptable? PR says: "if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies." So it's deliberate. But is 10s realistic for run registration? GitHub Actions run registration after a push typically appears within a few seconds to ~30s. Risk of spurious alarm is real but bounded — the issue auto-resolves the next day. I'd flag as SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT: consider waiting on `gh run watch`-style bounded wait (e.g., poll for the run up to a couple minutes) instead of a single 10s re-read, so a successful re-arm doesn't still file a manual-fix issue. Given the whole point is self-healing without operator noise, filing a "manual fix needed" issue when the fix already happened is a design wart. I'd classify IMPORTANT? The machine will file an issue that says "manual re-push required" — operator noise, but self-resolving. The PR explicitly accepted this ("the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged"). Given deliberate design + auto-resolution next daily, I'll file as SUGGESTION... hmm. "when in doubt start one level higher". The claim "the leg self-heals" is undermined if it then alarms anyway in the majority of cases. Actually wait — will it? After `git push` of the tag returns, the push event is already delivered to GitHub; the workflow run record typically appears in the API within ~5-15s. With read_sleep=10 then a fetch, it's borderline. The v1.0.557 release twin registered quickly. Eh. I'll make it a SUGGESTION with the reasoning (poll for the run registration up to a minute instead of one fixed 10s re-read), since PR CI and next-daily re-verify bound the blast radius.

Seventh: Also consider — `rearm_tag` re-cut uses local tag ref fetched `--depth 1`. If the tag on the remote is a lightweight tag (v1.0.558 case!), `git rev-parse "$tag^{commit}"` works; `git tag -a -f` creates annotated over lightweight → converts it. PR description covers this (v1.0.558 lightweight gets re-armed as annotated). But note: converting a lightweight tag to annotated changes `%(creatordate)` semantics — fine.

Eighth: `git tag -a -f "$tag"` when the local ref was fetched to `refs/tags/$tag` — fine.

Ninth: **race — `emit "published=$published"` vs new success path**: In the new success branch it emits `published=$fresh` (good). 

Tenth: **`echo "::error::...still serves $fresh (was $published)"`** — fine.

Eleventh: test file — `rearm-registers` test asserts `r.inFlight` isTrue: the re-armed run is queued with PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS=2 → terminal-wait polls twice → still queued → in_flight. gh run view of run 4242: plantRun('thirdReadJson') created run-4242.json with status queued (listed != completed → base = '{"status":"queued","conclusion":null}'). The terminal-wait loop: `gh run view ... --json status` → queued; polls: attempts = poll_attempts(900) with poll_sleep=0 → a=max_polls=2 → two polls, both queued → in_flight "still queued". exitCode 0. Good.

But wait — in that test the gh stub for `gh run list` third read: runs-v0.1.497.3.json planted via thirdReadJson. The stub serves .2.json on second call, .3.json on third? Presumably stub logic: first call → runs-vX.json, second → .2.json, third → .3.json, then stays at last. Need to check the gh stub for how it counts list reads — it matched `hasLength(3)` for `--branch` invocations in the not-registered test where thirdReadJson is null: initial, .2.json (second), third call → falls back to .2.json again? The count assertion is just on invocation count (3), not content. Fine.

Twelfth: **`git push --force` to the bare origin in the sandbox** — `rearmPushTo: 'origin'` pushes via the stubbed git? The script calls `git` — in tests, PATH has stub bin first; does the git stub forward to FA_REAL_GIT for non-stubbed subcommands? Presumably (FA_REAL_GIT exists for that). Since the rearm tests were claimed 27/27 in the hand replica and PR CI will run them, acceptable. But I can actually RUN the bash-level test myself! The dart harness can't run (dart SIGKILL), but I can replicate... that's what the author did. PR CI is the gate. I can at least run `bash -n` (done, OK).

Can I run dart? Let me try quickly to see if I can actually run the test suite... The PR says the host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM. Try `dart --version` with a short timeout. Worth a shot — if it works, run the race test.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +252
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#
# States (gh-1192; refined by #1368 — the 2026-10-07 false alarm; gh-1522):
#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for

#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays

#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag
# has a fresh run the moment it is visible, so the classification reads the
# run, never the stale tag age, and a completed fresh run verifies normally.
#
# gh-1561: the never-triggered arms first try to RE-ARM — the tag is
# force-re-pushed (SAME commit, fresh annotated tag object: a new tag-push
# event the leg could not otherwise produce) with the fa-release-bot App
# token (RELEASE_APP_TOKEN — the only credential class whose pushes
# cascade, gh-1172), and the fresh push run re-enters this flow. A push run
# that completes during the leg re-reads pub.dev before any «did not
# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.
#
# E2: only the LATEST tag is evaluated; stale older tags are out of scope.
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound
read_sleep="${PUBDEV_READ_SLEEP_SECS:-10}"  # test seam (production: 10s)
poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal
max_polls="${PUBDEV_MAX_POLLS:-90}"         # iteration cap (bounds the waits in tests)
#
# Budget vs the pubdev leg's 60m ceiling (daily-publish.yml): the waits can
# STACK — terminal-wait 900s + bounded rerun watch 900s + post-rerun verify
# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m
# more), so the rerun watch is capped at 15m, not 20m. A job killed at 60m
# is a CANCELLED leg the report files as a watcher death — the «past any
# budget → neutral skip, never an error» guarantee must survive end-to-end
# (#1370 review).

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

# poll_attempts: iteration count for a bounded wait — a sleep-based budget
# (wait/sleep, capped), or the fixed cap when sleeps are disabled in tests.
poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a
  if [ "${poll_sleep}" -gt 0 ]; then
    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else
    a="$max_polls"
  fi
  if [ "$a" -gt "$max_polls" ]; then a="$max_polls"; fi
  if [ "$a" -lt 1 ]; then a=1; fi

# pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder. The `pubspec=` output key name is
# kept (daily-publish report consumers read it), its value is the tag

  | grep -v '\^' | awk '{print $2}' | sed 's|refs/tags/||' \
  | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | sort -V | tail -1 || true)
pubspec="${latest_remote_tag#v}"
emit "pubspec=$pubspec"
emit "published=" # re-exported below after query

  echo "::notice::pubspec declares publish_to: none — package is private, nothing to verify on pub.dev"
  exit 0

  echo "::notice::no vX.Y.Z tags on the remote — nothing has been released yet, nothing to verify on pub.dev"

newest=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$pubspec" "$published" | sort -V | tail -1)

fi

tag="v$pubspec"

concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +252
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the

# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired
# bump-commit flow's «tag not cut yet / bump on main» states are gone:
# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the
# appear-wait branch is deleted as impossible.
#
# The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
# accepts OIDC only from tag-push runs — the release-event twin of a tag can
# never publish, #1368). This script VERIFIES pub.dev serves the tag
# version and, when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push
# publish run — a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims.
# Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an issue with a
# manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
#

#   up-to-date          pub.dev already serves the latest tag version
#   release-in-flight   the publish outcome is NOT yet observable — neutral
#                       skip (no ::error::, no auto-filed issue); the next
#                       scheduled daily re-verifies. Covers:
#                         · tag exists but its ci.yml run is not visible yet
#                           and the tag is younger than the grace window
#                         · the tag's PUSH ci.yml run is queued/in_progress —
#                           the script waits up to RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS for

#                           waits for the publish conclusion, with a
#                           timeout); past the budget the outcome stays
#                           unobserved and the skip stays neutral — runner

#   recovered           the failed tag-push publish run was re-run and
#                       pub.dev caught up
#   private             publish_to: none — nothing to verify
# Alarms — each error says WHICH state (Never-again #2):
#   «never triggered (only release-event run(s) …)»  — pub.dev OIDC rejects
#                       release-event tokens, so those runs cannot publish
#   «never triggered (no run registered past the grace window)»
#   «publish did not upload» — the push run went green but pub.dev still
#                       serves the old version
#
# E4: the «re-push the tag» manual fix keeps working — a re-pushed old tag

# upload» verdict — the start-of-leg read is stale for it. Without the
# token the manual-re-push alarms stay exactly as they were.

out="${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?GITHUB_OUTPUT must be set}"
grace="${RELEASE_FLIGHT_GRACE_SECS:-900}" # AC1: «no run at all» window bound

poll_sleep="${PUBDEV_POLL_SLEEP_SECS:-20}"  # test seam (production: 20s)
run_terminal_wait="${RUN_TERMINAL_WAIT_SECS:-900}"  # wait for the tag run to go terminal

# poll 600s ≈ 40m of the 60m wall (checkout + the spaced reads take ~2m

poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds
  local a

concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1566
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1566
- **Title**: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1561-daily-publish-pubdev` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +252
- **Deletions**: -6
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T10:57:01Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. # pr-1566: fix(1561): daily pubdev leg self-heals a never-triggered tag via App-token re-push

## Description

Fixes #1561

## Root cause (file:line-grounded)

The 05:35Z daily (`daily-publish.yml` run 38208595176, job 114677581867, step `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`) failed with:

```
pubspec=1.0.557 published=1.0.556
##[error]v1.0.557 has no ci.yml run — the tag-publish never triggered (only non-push run(s) exist — the publish job fires on push-event tag runs only).
```

Timeline (all verified via API/logs):

- v1.0.555 (Oct 11 14:48Z) and v1.0.556 (Oct 11 18:51Z): both tags have a **push + release run pair**; the App-token tag push from ci.yml's release job cascaded, the push twin's `publish` job (event-gated `github.event_name == 'push'`, ci.yml:3173-3205) uploaded to pub.dev. 1.0.556 is live on pub.dev.
- `v1.0.557` (annotated, points at bfb65bd) was cut at 03:12:07Z by `fa-release-bot[bot]` inside the 02:57:51Z schedule run's `Auto-release (tag cut)` job (job 114647325044, 03:11:48→03:12:12). The tag landed on the remote and `gh release create` fired the release twin (run 38198824498, success) — but the **push twin never registered**. Same App token, same script, identical to the two cascades 8-12h earlier: a GitHub-side tag-push trigger anomaly (the push event either never fired or never matched), not an in-repo regression — v1.0.556..bfb65bd touched only job-level classifier steps, not the `on:` block.
- The owner then created/published release **v1.0.558** (draft 03:07:08Z, published 05:37:33Z) — a server-side-created **lightweight** tag at the same commit bfb65bd. Tags created via the Releases API never fire push events, so v1.0.558 has only a release twin too and cannot publish either. It is now the LATEST tag, so tomorrow's daily would alarm identically.

The leg's design can detect this state but not heal it: only a push-event run can publish (pub.dev OIDC rejects release-event tokens, #1368), a rerun keeps the original event, and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push never cascades (gh-1172).

## Delivered

- **`scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`** — the never-triggered arms now attempt a **re-arm** before alarming (`rearm_tag()`): the latest tag is force-re-pushed at the **same peeled commit** as a fresh annotated tag object (new tagger date → new oid → a real tag-push event; a same-oid push is a no-op), authenticated with the fa-release-bot App token (`RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`) — the same credential mechanism ci.yml's release job uses to cut tags. The fresh push run re-enters the existing E4 flow (terminal-wait → publish → pub.dev poll); if it isn't registered after one spaced re-read, the manual-fix alarm fires unchanged and the next daily re-verifies.
- Same flow, adjacent pre-existing hazard fixed: a push run that **completes during the leg** (re-armed tag or the E4 operator re-push) is green only after its publish job verified pub.dev, so the stale start-of-leg read must not produce a false «publish did not upload» verdict — the success branch now re-reads pub.dev (3 spaced reads) and reports `up-to-date` green on catch-up.
- **`.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`** — the pubdev leg mints a job-scoped App token (`actions/create-github-app-token` @ the same pin as ci.yml's release job; `RELEASE_APP_ID`/`RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets already exist) and passes it as `RELEASE_APP_TOKEN`. Job `permissions` unchanged (contents: read, actions: write); without the secret the script fails over to the existing manual-fix alarm.
- **`test/release_flow_race_test.dart`** — new `gh-1561` group: re-arm registers the fresh run (neutral skip, tag re-cut at the same commit asserted via the origin's tagger date), re-armed run completes during the leg + pub.dev catches up → `up-to-date` green, failed re-arm push → unchanged manual alarm with no extra reads, re-arm pushed but run not yet registered → alarm with exactly one re-read; plus a curl read-count fixture seam (`pubdev-switch-after`) modeling CDN catch-up mid-leg.

## Remaining

- The one-off event drop itself is GitHub-side; the owner's v1.0.558 lightweight tag needs no action — the next armed daily (or a manual leg dispatch, SM's call) will re-arm v1.0.558, its fresh push run publishes 1.0.558, and the issue auto-closes green. v1.0.557 is superseded and intentionally left unpublished (E2: only the latest tag is evaluated).

## Local gate (honest disclosure)

The host guard SIGKILLs the dart VM (exit 137 on `dart --version`), so the dart suite could not run locally. Fallback: (1) `bash -n` on the script and a structural delta check of the test file vs HEAD (brace/paren deltas +17/+17 and +87/+87 — every replaced block internally balanced; imports/directive order untouched, no new imports needed, all new symbols defined in-file); (2) the script's behavior was verified end-to-end with a hand-driven replica of the test sandbox (bare origin + backdated annotated tag + shallow job clone + gh/curl stubs with Nth-read and read-count fixtures): **27/27 assertions pass** across the four new scenarios and the no-token/release-twin regressions, including byte-identical legacy alarm text and read counts. PR CI is the real gate for the dart file.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verify pub.dev serves the LATEST TAG version — the daily-publish pubdev
# leg's check (gh-1192, reworked gh-1522). Extracted verbatim from the
# inline step in daily-publish.yml so the classification is shell-harness
# testable (fake gh/curl fixtures, test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
#
# gh-1522: the git tag is the single source of truth — the committed
# pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder, so the version under test is
# the LATEST REMOTE TAG (git ls-remote), never a file read. The retired

# the version IS a tag that exists on the remote by construction, so the

emit() { printf '%s\n' "$1" >> "$out"; }

poll_attempts() { # $1 = wait seconds

    a=$(( $1 / poll_sleep ))
  else

concurrency:
      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the tag push rides the
    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in
    # the run.
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      # Job-scoped App token (gh-1172 fix-contract item 1): minted per run,
      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push + `gh release create`, nothing else.
          permissions: contents:write

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # gh-1477: blobless — tag math reads commit metadata only.
          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

      - name: Cut release tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh release create rides the App token (gh-1172): without an
          # explicit GH_TOKEN the create || true in auto_release.sh would be
          # a guaranteed silent no-op and the curated notes would never reach
          # the release object.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh
